rubrics.rubric: Does the grade calculation correctly apply the weighting scheme from the grading rubric, with completed components (Attendance & Participation 15%, Reading Response 1 5%, Research Proposal 10%, Midterm Exam 15%) calculated and pending components (Midterm Paper 15%, Reading Response 2 5%, Final Research Paper 20%, Final Exam 15%) clearly marked?
criterion: The projected grade calculation uses the exact weights from the Grading_Criteria sheet: Attendance & Participation (15%, 150 points), Reading Response 1 (5%, 50 points), Research Proposal (10%, 100 points), and Midterm Exam (15%, 150 points).
The completed components (those with due dates on or before October 21, 2024) are calculated using actual student scores and their respective weights.
The Midterm Paper (due 2024-10-18) is included in the calculation only if it has been graded; otherwise it is treated as pending.
Components due after mid-October (Reading Response 2 due 2024-11-05, Final Research Paper due 2024-12-06, Final Exam due 2024-12-12) are clearly indicated as pending or not yet graded.
The weighting scheme across all eight components sums to 100% and each component's point allocation matches the Grading_Criteria sheet specifications.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response identify and document data anomalies in the attendance records, specifically addressing that 2024-11-28 falls on Thanksgiving Day when university classes are not held?
criterion: The response identifies that 2024-11-28 (Thanksgiving Day) is a federal holiday when university classes are not held, and flags this attendance record as a data quality issue.
The response explains why having an attendance record on a non-class day constitutes invalid data.
The response describes how this anomaly affects attendance calculations (e.g., excluding this date from attendance rate denominators).
The response may also flag 2024-11-26 if institutional policy indicates no classes during Thanksgiving week.

rubrics.rubric: Does the at-risk identification correctly apply all eight threshold criteria from the At_Risk_Criteria sheet with the exact thresholds: Attendance Rate <70%, Assignment Completion <75%, Current Grade <70%, Midterm Exam Score <60%, Participation Score <5/10 average, Missing Assignments >=2, Late Submissions >=3, and No Office Hours Visits after midterm?
criterion: All eight at-risk indicators from the At_Risk_Criteria sheet are evaluated: Attendance Rate <70%, Assignment Completion <75%, Current Grade <70%, Midterm Exam Score <60%, Participation Score <5/10 average, Missing Assignments >=2, Late Submissions >=3, and No Office Hours Visits after midterm (October 15, 2024).
Each indicator uses the exact threshold value specified in the At_Risk_Criteria sheet without modification.
Every student in the class roster is checked against all eight indicators to produce a complete at-risk matrix.
The 'after midterm' condition for Office Hours Visits is correctly interpreted as visits occurring after October 15, 2024.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response correctly identify watch list students who fall within 5% above each at-risk threshold (e.g., 70-75% attendance rate, 70-75% current grade, 60-65% midterm exam score)?
criterion: Watch list identification uses a 5% buffer zone above each at-risk threshold: attendance rate 70-75%, current grade 70-75%, midterm exam score 60-65%, assignment completion 75-80%, and participation score 5.0-5.5 out of 10.
Students falling within these buffer zones are flagged separately from at-risk students as requiring monitoring.
The watch list designation is framed as a preventive measure to stop students from progressing to at-risk status.

rubrics.rubric: Does the sociological analysis correctly operationalize parental-education constructs using Medu and Fedu from student-por.csv, with defensible definitions and appropriate limits on any first-generation interpretation?
criterion: The analysis correctly interprets Medu (mother's education) and Fedu (father's education) from student-por.csv using the UCI coding scheme: 0=none, 1=primary education (4th grade), 2=5th-9th grade, 3=secondary education, 4=higher education.

The analysis states and justifies its Medu/Fedu grouping or coding rule and applies it to academic outcomes. A proxy for neither parent having higher education uses Medu <4 and Fedu <4 (equivalently, both 0-3); Medu <=1 and Fedu <=1 identifies parents with at most primary education and must not be presented as the same construct. Other explicit operationalizations receive credit only when their labels and rationale match the UCI codes and their use in the analysis is demonstrated.

The response acknowledges the limits of the chosen parental-education measure: Portuguese secondary-school records cannot establish actual first-generation U.S. college-student status. Any first-generation interpretation must be explicitly qualified as a proxy, not an observed identity.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response include explicit methodological caveats acknowledging that student-por.csv represents Portuguese secondary school students, not American university students, limiting direct applicability?
criterion: The response explicitly states that student-por.csv is from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and contains Portuguese secondary school student data.
The analysis of student-por.csv data acknowledges that this is a different educational level (secondary vs. postsecondary) and a different country/cultural context (Portugal vs. USA).
The response notes that variables like studytime, famsize (GT3/LE3), Pstatus (T/A), and grades (G1, G2, G3 on a 0-20 scale) may not translate directly to the SOCI201 context.
Findings from the student-por.csv analysis are framed as general sociological patterns that may inform but not directly predict SOCI201 student outcomes.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Excel deliverable (SOCI201_EarlyAlert_Week10.xlsx) clearly contain the four required content areas—projected grades with data quality documentation, an at-risk student matrix, composite risk scores with calculations, and a watch list—without requiring an exact sheet count or order?
criterion: The workbook includes all four required content areas in a clear layout; projected grades and data quality documentation may be combined or placed on separate sheets, and exact sheet count and order are not required.
One or more sheets include all students' projected grades with individual component scores and data quality flags or documentation.
A clearly identified sheet or section contains a matrix showing which of the eight at-risk criteria each student triggers.
A clearly identified sheet or section presents composite risk scores with visible priority-weighted calculation methodology.
A clearly identified sheet or section lists watch list students (those within 5% of at-risk thresholds).

rubrics.rubric: Does the response cross-validate assignment submission dates against due dates to identify late submissions (Reading Response 1 due 2024-09-10, Research Proposal due 2024-09-27, Midterm Paper due 2024-10-18)?
criterion: Data validation compares submitted_date values in the assignments table against due_date values for each assignment.

The due dates used are: Reading Response 1 (Mills' Sociological Imagination) due 2024-09-10, Research Proposal (Social Inequality Topic) due 2024-09-27, and Midterm Paper (Stratification Analysis) due 2024-10-18.
Submissions where submitted_date exceeds due_date are flagged as late.
Missing submitted_date values are identified as incomplete/unsubmitted assignments.
